_README.purpose: CALIBRATION REFERENCE ONLY. These are official ETS TOEFL Essentials 'Listen and Reply' items, extracted verbatim from ETS's own free practice test. They exist in this repo solely so that the QC gates in scripts/study-bank/ can be calibrated against a known-good corpus instead of against our own defective items.

permitted: Measuring our QC gates against it (blind-solve margin, key-slot spread, length rank, batch variety).
Reading it to understand what the real task type actually looks like.

provenance.method: The practice test is a single self-contained HTML application. The item bank is embedded as tab-delimited literals assigned to the JS variable `fv` (rows tagged "listqr"). Fields, per the engine's own parser at calcIcon_get_info_67411: 1=type, 2=audio index, 3=picture index, 4=intro text, 5=stem (the spoken utterance), 6-9=the four options. The keyed option is the one suffixed with '@', which the engine strips before display.
authenticity: 30 listqr rows, audio indices 1..30, matched 1:1 by 30 <audio> elements in the same file.
Audio index 1 is named soundIcon_whofav_*, matching stem 1 'Who's your favorite basketball player?'.
Pearson r between stem word count and the engine's data-medialength (audio seconds) is 0.715 over the 30 items, so the stem text is the transcript of the audio, not an unrelated field.
All 30 rows have exactly 9 fields, exactly one '@'-marked option, and 4 distinct options.
Practice tests 1, 2 and 3 differ only in navigation targets; the Listening item pool is byte-identical across all three, so 30 is the entire published pool, not a third of it.
provenance.classification: GENUINE OFFICIAL ETS. Not a third-party imitation. Nothing in this file was written, paraphrased, reconstructed or completed by a model.

_README.matchesLedgerBaseline: ledger.json records baseline task=choose_response, label 'ETS TOEFL Essentials - official', source 'ets.org free practice test 1', n=30. The n and the source both match, so this is very likely the exact corpus whose scores (mean 62.2, control 36.7, margin 25.5) were kept when the item text was discarded.
caveats: ETS calls the section directions 'Listen and Reply'; the on-screen prompt is 'Choose the best response.'
No difficulty labels, no explanations, and no per-item statistics are published. Only stimulus, options and key.

This is a familiarization test. ETS states on the welcome screen: 'this test is not a simulation of the TOEFL Essentials test'. Treat difficulty as indicative, not as the operational form's difficulty.

notesForOurBrief: Official stimuli are 5-12 words (mean 8.2). CHOOSE-A-RESPONSE-BRIEF.md mandates 12-28 words. Every one of our items is longer than the longest official one.
Official stimuli are overwhelmingly bare questions or short statements. There is no two-clause concession anywhere in the 30; our live cohort is ~94% concession-shaped.
Key length rank is 10/9/2/9 across ranks 1-4, i.e. NOT flat and skewed toward the LONGEST option. Our brief's 25/25/25/25 target is stricter than the real form.
Longest/shortest option ratio reaches 2.9x; our brief caps it at 1.6x. Real items do not obey that cap.
Distractors are frequently off-topic word-echoes ('I like it plain, thanks' for 'plane'), which our VERBAL-DISTRACTOR-CONSTRAINT would reject.
Settings repeat freely (several shopping/travel items); the brief's 'no scenario twice' rule is stricter than the real form.
descriptives.stimulusIsQuestion: 29/30 (the one exception is item 8, a plain statement)
descriptives.widePivotRate: 0/30 = 0.0%. check-batch-variety.mjs's wide-pivot regex fires on ZERO official items, against 94.4% of our live choose_response cohort and 100% of nearmiss-v1. This is the single most useful number in this file: it is a real control for that gate.
